extracted.intended_audience: scholars, students, instructors, and librarians interested in humor studies/folklore
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptions and publisher blurbs that articulate what makes scholarly work on humor and folklore valuable — methodological standards, pedagogical qualities, theoretical contributions, and stylistic expectations for academic books and anthologies about humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of a scientific perspective in folkloristics
rubrics_metrics.description: "While recognizing the study of jokes and other forms of folklore as a humanistic endeavor, Oring believes in the relevance of a scientific perspective to the enterprise. He values clear definitions, tests of hypotheses and theories, empirical evidence, experiment, and the search for laws.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance emphasizes privileging clear definitions, hypothesis-testing, empirical evidence and experiment; treat folklore scholarship as amenable to scientific-style inquiry and law-seeking rather than purely impressionistic interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible yet sophisticated writing
rubrics_metrics.description: "Written in a sophisticated yet accessible style, The Consolations of Humor and Other Folklore Essays stimulates both scholars and students alike...",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books should balance scholarly rigor with readability: accessible prose that still addresses advanced issues so the work serves both students and scholars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual (not content-only) analysis of humorous expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: "He provides alternate ways of thinking about humorous expressions by examining their contexts--not just their contents.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate analyses by how well they situate jokes and humorous forms within social, historical, and interactional contexts rather than treating texts in isolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze incongruity/absurdity as mechanisms with communicative ends
rubrics_metrics.description: "He also shows how the incongruity and absurdity essential to the production of laughter can serve serious communicative ends.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion asks that accounts trace how formal features (incongruity, absurdity) produce laughter and how those features function to communicate meanings or social positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of diverse examples and genres
rubrics_metrics.description: (implied by listing) "classic Jewish jokes, frontier humor, racist cartoons, blonde jokes, and Internet humor",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong work samples humor across multiple genres, media, and cultural traditions to support comparative claims; breadth of exemplars strengthens generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat humor as meaningful social expression (identity, sentimentality, national formation)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Engaging Humor examines the thoughts that underlie jokes, the question of racist motivation in ethnic humor, and the use of humor as a commentary on social interaction... explores the relationship between humor and sentimentality and the role of humor in forging national identity.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the work addresses humor's social functions, including identity formation, sentimentality, and commentary on interaction and power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introductory texts should give a solid sense of major topics and interpretive techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: "Oring's introductory folklore text consists of a series of essays by leading scholars that give the student a solid sense of major folklore topics and interpretive techniques.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textbooks/introductory books should comprehensively cover core topics and methods, be suitable for classroom use, and meet instructional needs over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anthologies/readers should extend discussion and introduce alternative perspectives and be pedagogically organized
rubrics_metrics.description: "Compiled to accompany the best-selling textbook... the selections in this anthology extend the discussion in diverse directions, alert the reader to new problems, and introduce alternative perspectives... organized in sections that correspond to the chapter headings in An Introduction.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for readers: selections should broaden and complicate textbook themes, raise new problems, introduce divergent viewpoints, and be organized to align with teaching modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confront problems and address controversial topics with empirical data and insights
rubrics_metrics.description: "Joking Asides... confronts the problems of humor, analyzing the key contemporary approaches to its study and addressing controversial topics with new empirical data and insights.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality scholarship explicitly tackles open/controversial issues and supports positions with empirical evidence and novel insights rather than mere assertion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propose and test theoretical frameworks against competing accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: "A folklorist drawn to the study of humor, Oring developed his formulation of 'appropriate incongruity' as a frame to understand what jokes must do to produce humor. He tests appropriate incongruity against other major positions in the field, including the general theory of verbal humor, conceptual integration theory, benign violation theory, and false-belief theory.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works should articulate clear theoretical frameworks and evaluate them comparatively against alternative theories, using empirical or argumentative tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: "Oring draws on the work of scholars from several disciplines—anthropology, folklore, philosophy, psychology, linguistics, and literature...",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuable work integrates perspectives and findings from multiple disciplines relevant to humor, demonstrating cross-disciplinary awareness and synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze construction, evolution, targets, and artistic qualities of jokes and performances
rubrics_metrics.description: "...to ask basic questions about the construction and evolution of jokes, untangle the matter of who the actual targets of a joke might be, and characterize the artistic qualities of jokes and joke performances.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate treatments of joke structure, historical/folkloric change, identification of targets/audiences, and aesthetic/performative dimensions of joking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous theoretical exploration, critical engagement, and original observation
rubrics_metrics.description: "A major work from a major scholar, Joking Asides is a rigorous exploration of theoretical approaches to jokes and their functions and is filled with disquieting questions, penetrating criticisms, and original observations.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality scholarship should offer rigorous theory work, critical scrutiny of existing approaches, and original contributions that advance understanding rather than summarize prior work.
